decision.recommended_plan: No tension exists between the two recommendations, so both can be adopted as given. Cost recommends funding the full day-one cost of 345,062.73 USD (rather than phasing), noting the six nonzero cost gaps (NYX-001, 006, 007, 012, 013, 016) are moderate and reasonably evenly distributed, so a phased schedule would add administrative overhead without meaningful budget relief. Retention independently evaluated the three underwater employees (NYX-001, NYX-007, NYX-013, all below the 0.85 compa-ratio threshold) and, based on role scope and seniority evidence, did not flag any of them as organizationally critical -- all three read as backfillable, junior-to-developing contributors rather than irreplaceable talent. Because cost's own recommendation is day-one (not phased) funding for the full population, including all three underwater employees, there is no scenario here where a critical employee would be left underwater during an unfunded phase-in period -- both because cost isn't proposing to phase, and because retention flagged nobody as critical in the first place. The two recommendations are complementary: fund the full 345,062.73 USD cost-gap correction at close per the cost agent, and separately fund the 220,759.99 USD retention award (also day-one per retention's own schedule) for the three underwater-but-non-critical employees to address pay compression through standard means, as retention itself recommends. No conflicting positions to reconcile.
